title: Platform systems & services: ops playbook, dashboards, runbooks, retrospective, and roadmap (Addendum)
author: Michael Chen
body:
Summary

This addendum consolidates platform systems & services operational best practices: a concise runbook for high-impact oncall incidents, the current dashboards & alerting baseline, a short retrospective of Q2-Q3 2026 operational changes, and the roadmap items we will prioritize through Q1 2027. It is intended for the platform team, SREs, and cross-functional stakeholders who own observability, capacity, and incident response for Redwood's inference platform.

Scope

- Applies to the Platform Systems & Services stack: routing/gateway, control plane services, autoscaling controllers, metric ingestion pipelines, and core dashboards used by oncall.
- Excluded: customer-specific Private deployments (see eng-private-deployments onprem-packaging).

Owner & escalation

- Primary owner: Platform Systems & Services team (oncall alias: platform-oncall@redwood.internal).
- Secondary support: Eng-SRE (sre-support@redwood.internal).
- Pager escalation: follow standard oncall rotation - 15 min ack, 30 min mitigation, 60 min exec notification. See oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process.

SLOs & key metrics (summary)

- Control plane API availability (prod): 99.95% monthly.
- Gateway 99th p95 token latency (in-region): < 650ms for small models; < 1500ms for large models.
- Request success rate (5m window): >= 99.5% (includes 4xx and 5xx filtering per severity policy).
- Metric ingestion latency (prometheus -> long-term store): 0-2 minutes 95th.

Dashboards (baseline panels to include)

Note: these are the canonical panels we maintain in Grafana for platform oncall. Dashboard folders: /dashboards/platform/control-plane, /dashboards/platform/gateway, /dashboards/platform/capacity.

1) Control Plane Overview (grafana id: PLT-CP-01)
- API call rate (rps) per service (controlplane-gateway, route-manager, rollout-controller).
- 5xx rate and 4xx rate (per service).
- Error budget burn (30d).
- Leader election / controller-manager status (boolean).
- Active rollouts / canaries in-progress.

2) Gateway / Inference Frontend (PLT-GW-01)
- Request latency histograms (p50/p90/p95/p99) split by model-size bucket.
- CPU/GPU utilization on serving nodes (aggregate by pool).
- Connection churn / refused connections.
- Prefix cache hit ratio and kv-cache eviction rate.

3) Autoscaler & Capacity (PLT-CAP-01)
- Pending pods/instances vs. desired replicas.
- Scale events (succeeded/failed) and reason.Timestamps.
- Provisioning time distribution (minutes).
- GPU pool cold-start incidents count.

Alerting (recommended rules & thresholds)

We enforce pragmatic alert levels to reduce noise: SEV1 (pager) for production-impacting failures, SEV2 (email + Slack) for degradations, SEV3 (ticket) for non-urgent anomalies.

Critical alert examples (SEV1)
- Control plane API 5xx rate > 5% for 5m across >2 services -> pager.
- Gateway p99 latency > 3s for 5m for production cluster -> pager.
- Autoscaler failure: scale operation error rate > 2 errors / 5m -> pager.
- Leader election loss (controller-manager) -> pager.

Degraded alert examples (SEV2)
- Request success rate drop > 1% (5m) -> Slack + ticket.
- Cache hit ratio < 60% sustained > 10m -> Slack.
- Metric ingestion lag > 3m -> Slack.

Operational runbook: SEV1 gateway high latency

1) Triage (first 5 minutes)
  a) Acknowledge the page. Post to #platform-oncall with incident template: summary, first-observed, current impact, mitigation in progress.
  b) Open Dashboard PLT-GW-01. Collect: p95/p99 trends, per-pool latency, recent deploys (last 30m), autoscaler events.

2) Rapid mitigation (5-20 minutes)
  a) If one pool shows disproportionate latency: move traffic away via routing policy (route-manager -> set weight 0 on pool). Use CLI: rctl route update --route <route> --remove-pool <pool-id>.
  b) If memory/CUDA OOM on serving nodes: set pool health to drain and scale up a healthy pool. Command: kctl label node <node> pool=drain; autoscaler allow-scale --pool <healthy-pool> --reason "oom mitig".
  c) If the issue is broad and model-sensitive, fallback to a lower-cost model variant (refer to model-catalog).

3) Restore & confirm (20-60 minutes)
  a) Validate SLO metrics are back to baseline for at least 10 minutes.
  b) If mitigation required traffic changes, schedule canary re-enable with 5-10% ramp over 10 minutes.
  c) Capture mitigation steps in the incident ticket.

4) Post-incident (owner within 48 hours)
  a) Create a short incident summary in oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems.
  b) Run retrospective checklist (see section below).

Standard runbook commands (examples)

- Check recent deploys: gitopsctl history --service gateway --since 30m
- Inspect pods: kctl get pods -n platform -l app=gateway -o wide
- Read logs (last 2m): kctl logs -n platform <pod> --since 2m | grep "ERROR"
- Force drain: rctl pool set-health --pool <id> --health DRAINING --reason "oncall mitigation"

Retrospective: Q2-Q3 2026 (summary of operational learnings)

Key wins -
- Reduced noisy SEV2 paging by tuning cache-hit alerts and introducing a 10m sustained window.
- Improved autoscaler heuristics: new cooldown heuristics reduced oscillations by 28% across GPU pools.
- Introduced prefix KV cache telemetry which reduced average p99 latency for small-model requests by 12%.

Open improvements / action items
1) Observability: instrument rollout-controller with span IDs propagated into log lines by Q4 2026 (owner: eng-platform; ETA: 2026-11-30).
2) Capacity: evaluate predictive scaling prototype (ML-backed) for top-5 accounts by Q1 2027 (owner: eng-sre + product).
3) Runbooks: codify more automated mitigations (traffic-weight rollback) and add to bot-playbooks (owner: eng-developer-experience; ETA: 2026-12-15).

Roadmap (prioritized items through Q1 2027)

1) Q4 2026: Observability completeness
- Add distributed tracing on rollout paths, instrument route-manager.
- Consolidate dashboards into two canonical views to reduce cognitive load for oncall.

2) Q1 2027: Capacity & cost controls
- Pilot predictive autoscaling for selected GPU pools; measure cost savings & SLO impact.
- Add automated pre-warming for cold GPU pools in target regions.

3) Q1 2027: Runbook automation
- Implement safe-guarded traffic cutover automation (bot executes traffic-weight change after two-step confirmation).
- Add automated report generation for incident postmortems (pre-fill timeline & metrics).

Team wiki & knowledge transfer

- Keep living notes in the platform-team wiki (folder: /confluence/eng-platform/platform-team-wiki-runbooks-dashboards-roadmap).
- New joiners: mandatory 1-week onboarding playbook includes walkthrough of three dashboards (PLT-CP-01, PLT-GW-01, PLT-CAP-01), a simulated game-day, and runbook practice.

Document maintenance & review cadence

- This page owner (Michael Chen) will review quarterly or after any SEV1 incident with >4h customer impact.
- Review checklist: alert threshold efficacy, false-positive rate, runbook accuracy (commands), dashboard completeness.

Appendix A — Alert tuning cookbook (examples)

- To reduce false positives for gateway latency, replace single-point p99 alert with a composite: p99 > 2.5s for 5m AND p95 increased > 30% vs baseline 30m median.
- For autoscaler errors, add a rate limiter: only alert if error_count / scale_attempts > 0.15 for 5m.

Appendix B — Incident template (Slack)

Title: [SEV{level}] <short description> — <service>
Severity: SEV1 / SEV2
First observed: <timestamp>
Impact: <summary of customer impact (routes/models affected)>
Current status: <what mitigations executed>
Actions needed: <who / next steps>
Links: <dashboards>, <runbook>, <ticket>

Appendix C — Quick links & commands

- Dashboards: https://grafana.internal/d/PLT-CP-01, PLT-GW-01, PLT-CAP-01
- Incident tracker: https://incident.internal/ (create ticket with tag platform-oncall)
- Routing CLI: rctl (help: rctl --help)
- K8s CLI alias: kctl (help: kctl --help)

If you have suggested improvements to this playbook or need a custom dashboard for a product team, file a ticket in the platform-team board or email platform-ops@redwood.internal.
